# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-14 (Extended v118)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Summer Year 4, late afternoon ~5:30 P.M.)**: Paris—Café Musain near Panthéon; le Petit-Picpus convent district; M. Gillenormand's residences; Gorbeau house (50-52, Salpêtrière district); Luxembourg gardens (Rue de l'Ouest side); village of Austerlitz near Salpêtrière; English provincial towns (Dunstead, Kelmere, Torton, Ostcombe, Ravenmere, Kelford, Yarlby, Staveford, Gulhaven); Wilwick; Sceaux (ball location); Père-Lachaise cemetery; Rue Mouffetard; Rue De la Barrière-des-Gobelins; harbor towns of Dunstead and Kelford; Rue Gracieuse; Rue Pierre-Lombard; Rue Petit-Gentilly; Rue du Petit-Banquier. **Environmental progression**: Spring—frost silvering hedges, light early, smoke flat; Summer—warm air, sparrows chirping, bees humming in lavender, gulls quarrying, salt and tar scent from water, wind off water carries salt and tar, chimneys smoking flat, evening light early; **Autumn/Winter transition**: icy breeze through windows, snow falling, Candlemas sun promising snow that arrives, outer mist penetrating like whitish wadding, bell for vespers ringing thinly; **Current (late afternoon)**: Snow ceased then resumed, day declining, roads rutted and puddled after thaw.

## Primary Locations
**LUXEMBOURG GARDENS**: Fountain basin with swans; statues including Leonidas, Spartacus, Gladiator; "his alley" on Rue de l'Ouest side with recurring bench; bench by Gladiator near other end. **LE PETIT-PICPUS DISTRICT**: Number 62 Rue Petit-Picpus convent. **M. GILLENORMAND'S RESIDENCES**: Rue Férou; Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire. **GORBEAU HOVEL**: 50-52, Salpêtrière district; Marius's attic cabinet, 30 francs annually. **JONDRETTE DEN** (Summer Year 4): Within or near Gorbeau house; abject, dirty, fetid, sordid; furniture: straw chair, infirm table, crockery, two pallets; dormer window four panes draped in spiders' webs; leprous walls with seams and scars; obscene sketches in charcoal; repulsive moisture; let for forty francs yearly; floor uneven, antique plaster blackened; fireplace with brazier, pot, broken boards, suspended rags, bird-cage, ashes. Attic large with projections, angles, black holes, bays, promontories; horrible unfathomable nooks. One pallet near door, one near window. Colored engraving "THE DREAM" (black frame): sleeping woman and child, eagle in cloud with crown, woman thrusting crown away, Napoleon in glory on blue column with yellow capital. Wooden panel stood on ground against wall, picture-face turned to wall. Windows with broken panes. One bed occupied by Jondrette woman. Dark interior (newcomers experience cellar-like darkness; inhabitants accustomed to twilight). **Current state (late afternoon, Summer Year 4)**: Illuminated by sheet-iron brazier in fireplace filled with burning charcoal, glowing hot and red with blue flame. Verdigris candlestick with candle also burning. Chisel (large cold chisel with white wood handle, purchased from Rue Pierre-Lombard ironmonger's shop) thrust into brazier to heat. Two heaps visible: one of old iron, one of ropes. Interior resembles forge rather than hell-mouth; Jondrette in this light has air of demon rather than smith. Silence glacial and profound; no sound, no soul moving or speaking. **M. MABEUF'S COTTAGE**: Village of Austerlitz near Salpêtrière; thatched cottage; fifty crowns yearly; three rooms, enclosed garden.

## Jean Valjean and Cosette
Valjean integrated as assistant gardener in convent; inhabits old garden hut with Fauchelevent. Spiritual transformation complete. Cosette became convent scholar; believes Valjean is her father; adores him. Fauchelevent sole ally aware of full presence. Nuns unaware of circumstances. **Present state (Summer Year 4)**: Cosette about thirteen/fourteen years old; appeared in Jondrette hovel as charitable visitor with M. Leblanc distributing charity.

## Javert's Pursuit
Attached to Paris police after Valjean's escape. **Status (Winter Year 3)**: Established sentinels, organized traps around Gorbeau house; confident convict nearby. **Status (Summer Year 4, present)**: Tall man behind grating in commissary's office; leaning against stove, holding tails of vast topcoat with three collars. Face square, thin firm mouth, thick gray ferocious whiskers. Glance searches rather than penetrates; capable of turning pockets inside out. **Character**: Terrifying and reassuring simultaneously; inspires both fear and confidence. **Action (present, late afternoon Summer Year 4)**: Received report from Marius Pontmercy regarding Jondrette ambush plot. Gave Marius two small steel pistols ("knock-me-downs"), each loaded with two balls. Instructed Marius: hide in chamber to appear departed, watch through hole in wall, fire shot when matters reach crisis (not too soon), let men proceed toward execution then intervene. Javert entered one of most terrible hovels in Rue Gracieuse, remained quarter-hour, then purchased large cold chisel from Rue Pierre-Lombard ironmonger's shop. Proceeded rapidly to Rue du Petit-Banquier. At vicinity of wall where conspiracy was discussed, turned to ensure no follower, did not see Marius, sprang across wall and disappeared (planning ambush position).

## Marius Pontmercy: Development, Passion, and Crisis

**Identity and age**: Baron Marius Pontmercy, twenty years old (Spring Year 4); three years since left grandfather. **Paternal legacy**: Colonel's written instruction regarding baron title and Waterloo sergeant Thénardier. Lost medallion of black shagreen; believes grandfather burned it.

**Political evolution (Winter Year 3 → Spring Year 4)**: Converted to Bonapartism and republicanism; political fevers dissipated through reverie; Revolution of 1830 calmed views. Sympathies to humanity over nation, woman over people, idea over deed, poet over hero. Preferred introspection to action.

**Material condition (Spring Year 4)**: Gorbeau cabinet 30 francs annually; daily sustenance 20 sous (365 francs yearly); clothing 100 francs; linen/washing 100 francs. Total: 450 francs. Earned approximately seven hundred francs yearly. **Refused advancement (Winter Year 3)**: M. Magimel offered fifteen hundred francs yearly—Marius refused to preserve liberty and dignity. Deliberately stopped working to dedicate time to thought and meditation.

**Grandfather quarrel**: Violent estrangement three years ago without rapprochement—"Marius was the brass vase, while Father Gillenormand was the iron pot." Grandfather's suffering locked within breast.

**Relationship with Friends of the A B C**: Met Courfeyrac at Place Saint-Michel; became good friends. Did not enter decidedly into group but remained cordial. Close to **M. Mabeuf**—owed him revolution within soul; indebted for knowing and loving his father. **Recent social activities (Spring Year 4)**: Dined with Courfeyrac; breakfasted at Café Voltaire.

## The Mysterious Couple, Girl (Cosette), and Marius's Passion

**Initial six-month observation (over one year prior)**: Marius noticed man approximately sixty (M. Leblanc) and very young girl (thirteen/fourteen) on Luxembourg bench daily. Man: retired military officer, robust, weary, kindly; wore blue trousers and coat, broad-brimmed hat, black cravat, white shirt, white hair. Girl: thin, awkward, promise of handsome eyes; wore convent scholar dress.

**Six-month interruption**: Observation ceased for unknown reason.

**Reunion and girl's transformation (Summer Year 3)**: Girl became well-dressed young maiden. Wore black damask dress and cape, white crape bonnet, white gloves, carved Chinese ivory parasol handle, silken shoe.

**Marius's indifference (Summer Year 3)**: When she raised eyelids, Marius found only child's glance. She looked indifferently. Marius paid no further attention.

**First meaningful glance and awakening (Spring Year 4)**: On warm day in Luxembourg, their glances met. Marius perceived he wore everyday clothes; resolved to dress differently. Following day wore new coat, seated himself surveying her. Left only when gates closed. His worship of his father retreated to depths of soul.

**Marius's emotional transformation**: Love came. Brain felt on fire. She appeared beautiful, wholly feminine and angelic. Vexed about dust on boots. Followed her with eyes until disappeared. Walked like madman; ate and spoke excitedly; laughed uproariously.

**Strategic approach (Spring Year 4)**: Combined stations behind trees and pedestals with diplomacy to be seen by girl and unseen by M. Leblanc. Sometimes remained motionless half-hour in shade. She bent upon Marius all reveries of virginal and passionate eye.

**M. Leblanc's response**: Noticed something. Often rose when Marius arrived and moved to bench by Gladiator near other end. Marius did not pursue. M. Leblanc made daughter pass carriage entrance first, then stared intently at Marius.

**Escalation and handkerchief (Spring Year 4)**: Found handkerchief on bench after they left. Very simple, white, fine, exhaled ineffable perfume. Marked with letters U. F. Marius immediately thought "Ursule!" Kissed handkerchief, placed on heart during day; laid beneath lips at night.

**Leg incident and jealousy (Spring Year 4)**: Brisk May breeze lifted dress to height of garter. **A leg of exquisite shape appeared. Marius saw it. He was exasperated and furious.** Girl hastily thrust down dress with divinely troubled motion. Marius determined to be vexed. **Harsh and capricious jealousy of the flesh awakened in his heart.** When she passed bench, Marius darted sullen and ferocious glance. She gave slight straightening up with backward movement: "Well, what is the matter?"

**Veteran encounter and paroxysm**: A bent, wrinkled, pale veteran in Louis XV uniform bearing soldier's cross of Saint-Louis crossed walk. Marius thought he perceived man had extremely well satisfied air; struck him aged cynic addressed him fraternal and merry wink. **Marius reached paroxysm of jealousy.** "Perhaps he was there! Perhaps he saw!" Felt desire to exterminate the veteran.

**M. Leblanc and girl's disappearance (Summer-Autumn Year 4)**: Summer passed, autumn came, winter arrived. Neither set foot in Luxembourg garden again. **Marius had but one thought—to gaze once more on that sweet and adorable face.** Fell into black melancholy. All was over. Work disgusted him; walking tired him. Everything had disappeared.

**Self-reproach (Autumn Year 4)**: Heaped hundred reproaches on himself: "Why did I follow her? I was happy at mere sight! Why wish to have more?" Confided nothing to Courfeyrac, but Courfeyrac guessed everything.

**Ball at Sceaux (September Year 4)**: Allowed himself taken to ball hoping to find her. Did not see her. Left friends and returned home on foot alone through night, weary, feverish, with sad and troubled eyes.

**Miraculous rediscovery and action (Summer Year 4, afternoon)**: **Marius perceived the girl (Cosette) in Jondrette hovel when she arrived with M. Leblanc to distribute charity.** "It was certainly she. Marius could hardly distinguish her through the luminous vapor which had suddenly spread before his eyes. It was that sweet, absent being, that star which had beamed upon him for six months." **Marius shuddered in dismay, felt on brink of bursting into tears.** His heart palpitated; seemed to him he had lost his soul and just found it again. During entire visit, Marius lived in ecstasy; eyes remained fixed on girl; heart seized and wholly enveloped her from her very first step. Did not know sound of her voice. **He devoured her with his eyes. Could not believe divine creature was in midst of vile creatures in that monstrous lair. Seemed to him he beheld humming-bird in midst of toads.**

## The Jondrette Family and Ambush Plot—Present Crisis

**Current time: ~5:30 P.M., trap springs at 6 P.M.—30 minutes remaining.**

**Scheme and principals**: Jondrette arranged ambush. M. Leblanc will arrive at 6 o'clock to bring sixty francs (claimed as landlord payment). Accomplices include Panchaud (alias Printanier, alias Bigrenaille) and other prowlers of barriers. Location: Boulevard de l'Hôpital, house 50-52 (Gorbeau). **Preparation state (late afternoon)**: Brazier with charcoal glowing hot and red, blue flame flickering. Chisel heating in brazier. Two heaps prepared: old iron and ropes. Silence glacial and profound. Marius perceived in one attic the motionless heads of four men vaguely lighted by remnant of daylight through dormer window. **Marius's position (present, ~5:30 P.M.)**: Seated on his bed in adjoining chamber. Gave his key to inspector (Javert). Pistols concealed in trousers pockets. Cannot yet follow or warn M. Leblanc without exposing himself. Awaiting signal moment to fire shot. Experiences indescribable anxiety; hears beating of arteries like ticking watch in dark. Reflects on double march—crime advancing one side, justice coming other. Not afraid but shudders at what approaches. Entire day produces effect of dream; to persuade himself not in nightmare, feels cold barrels of steel pistols.

## Friends of the A B C, Patron-Minette, and Criminal Underground

**Friends of the A B C**: Declared themselves Friends of the A B C—_Abaissé_, the debased (the people). Secret society in embryonic state. Meetings back room Café Musain. Members: Enjolras, Combeferre, Jean Prouvaire, Feuilly, Courfeyrac, Bahorel, Lesgle/Laigle de Meaux, Joly, Grantaire. Most students; cordial with working classes.

**Philosophical discourse on social substructure**: All human societies have subterranean dimensions. Beneath social construction: religious, philosophical, economic, revolutionary mines. **The third lower floor (_le troisième dessous_)**: Below all mines, lies deepest stratum—**grave of shadows, cellar of blind, _Inferi_.** Wild spectres roam here, almost beasts, almost phantoms, unconcerned with universal progress. Two step-mothers: ignorance and misery. Guide: necessity. Satisfaction: appetite. Brutally voracious—ferocious as tiger. From suffering pass to crime. Man becomes dragon. Vault formed of ignorance. **All others above have one object—suppress it.** So long as society remains what it is, they remain what they are.

**Patron-Minette: Criminal association**: Members Babet, Gueulemer, Claquesous, Montparnasse. **Gueulemer**: Six feet high, Hercules of no defined position. Lair: sewer of Arche-Marion. Assassin through coolness. **Claquesous**: He was night. Emerged from hole at nightfall, returned before daylight. Hole location unknown. Addressed accomplices only in absolute darkness, back turned. If candle brought, put on mask. Ventriloquist. Never seen without mask. **Function**: Four ruffians formed Proteus, furnish canvas for ambushes in Seine department.

## English Provincial Towns: Mundane Activities and Confirmed Rumors

**Claims and rumors**: Lurald Stenworth told Thizek Stenenridge deed to Kelmere pastures forged (**confirmed by Lurald telling Ulrald Corrford**). Wenelle Lindmere drowned crossing estuary (rumor, no body). **Granary fire set on purpose (confirmed: Luena Stenenridge confided to Rozek that Dunstead granary fire was set on purpose; later Rozek confided to Pewyn Stenenridge that fire at Dunstead granary was set on purpose)**. Kadan Corrley burned letter from Yera Haskick revealing mill ledger rewritten. Kassa Brackick confided mill ledger rewritten. Fenelle Lindmere confided Stenson family once owed blood debt to Stenenridge family (**later Fenelle told Peten Haskick this**). Price of salt scandal discussed.

**Current mundane activities (Spring-Summer Year 4)**: Volan Stenworth and others read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half the saints; bought ribbon at stall and regretted it. Conversations about weather, harvest, lame horse, river up again in spring. Baker's boy late, line at oven long. Roads rutted and puddled after thaw. Smoke from chimneys lay flat over fields. Lurald spent evening sorting old letters by candlelight. Marald Corrford fell asleep in chair before fire. Nelan Brackick gave Volia Brackick solemn promise to repair roof of chapel at Wilwick.
